description: This pie chart illustrates the proportional distribution of various emotional states, likely in the context of evaluating speaker anonymization on emotional speech. The chart is divided into a total of six slices. The largest segment is colored light blue, labeled "Frustration," and accounts for 25.1% of the total. Moving clockwise, the next slice is purple, representing the "Neutral" category at 23.1%. This is followed by a medium blue slice labeled "Happiness," which is the smallest at 8.1%. Continuing clockwise, there is a red slice making up 14.1%; notably, the external text label for this specific segment is obscured by a solid grey rectangular block. Next is an orange slice labeled "Sadness" at 14.7%, and finally, a yellow slice representing "Anger" at 14.9%. The chart does not utilize a separate legend; instead, category labels are placed just outside the perimeter adjacent to their corresponding segments, while the exact percentage values are printed directly inside each slice. The segments do not appear to be ordered in a strict ascending or descending sequence based on size, and no individual slices are visually emphasized by being exploded, offset, or bolded.
